title: Extending the Subkey-Prediction Lemma to Larger Block Lengths
summary: Only the one-bit case is covered by the current subkey-prediction lemma; extending it to larger blocks with better bounds than the general lemma remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a big key modeled as a vector over $\{0,1\}^b$, where each probe returns one $b$-bit block or word, extend the subkey-prediction lemma currently established only for $b=1$ to larger block lengths $b$, and derive prediction bounds that improve on those obtainable from the previously available general lemma for larger $b$.

scope.domain: Mathematical foundations of big-key symmetric encryption and subkey prediction for block- or word-valued probes.
parameters: b: the block or word length returned by each probe
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the subkey-prediction lemma from the one-bit case to larger block lengths and derive bounds that improve on those from the available general lemma.

citations.label: Big-Key Symmetric Encryption: Resisting Key Exfiltration

progress.summary: The source states that the current subkey-prediction lemma handles only the one-bit case. It notes that a general lemma gives bounds for larger blocks, but expects an extension of the current lemma to yield better bounds and identifies obtaining it as an open question.
citation_labels: Mihir Bellare et al., Big-Key Symmetric Encryption: Resisting Key Exfiltration
